sras.def: Short-run aggregate supply: the total real output firms supply at each price level while nominal wages and some prices are fixed. The SRAS curve slopes up.

sticky-wages.def: Nominal wages (and some prices) that do not adjust right away when the price level changes, often because of contracts. They make SRAS slope up.

sras-shifter.def: A change in production costs at a given price level, such as input prices, productivity, taxes or subsidies on firms. A sudden economy-wide one is a supply shock.

long-run.def: The short run is the period in which nominal wages and some prices are fixed; the long run is long enough for all wages and prices to adjust.
